headline: Local Court Clerk Assigned To Transcribe IRCTC Case Trial Resigns After Realizing 'Audit Trail' Is Just A 400-Page Receipt For Railway Samosas
body:
The junior clerk at the Patiala House Court, assigned to digitize the exhaustive evidence files in the long-standing IRCTC case, formally requested a transfer this morning, citing a profound existential crisis triggered by the discovery that the primary financial ledger was actually a collection of discarded railway pantry invoices. 

'I spent three weeks categorizing what I thought were shell company transfers and complex offshore asset movements,' stated Ravi Kumar, a court stenographer who had been tasked with indexing the case documents. 'It turns out, the vast majority of the evidence is just a chronological list of 400,000 potato-filled pastries ordered between 2004 and 2006. The prosecution has been meticulously tracking the fluctuating price of chutney packets as if they were high-frequency trading algorithms.'

Legal experts are now scrambling to explain how a case involving major infrastructure contracts somehow evolved into an forensic inquiry regarding why certain railway routes were consistently under-supplied with ginger tea. Defense attorneys have reportedly filed a motion to have the entire proceedings reclassified as a 'Culinary History Archive,' arguing that the court is essentially holding a trial over the inflation-adjusted cost of a late-night snack service.

'My desk is currently buried under a stack of thermal paper that smells faintly of burnt oil and cumin,' added Kumar, while packing his office plant. 'I signed up to handle high-stakes white-collar crime, not to act as the primary historian for the catering standards of the Indian Railways. If I have to cross-reference one more invoice for a misplaced carton of milk, I am moving to a career in private arbitration, where the only thing they track is billable hours, not the structural integrity of a triangular snack.'
caption: When the high-stakes legal drama turns out to be a really expensive audit of a railway snack bar. #IRCTC #DelhiCourts #LegalDrama #SamosaEconomics (satire)
